messages:
sasha: Heads-up — I'm not able to stitch traces for a set of GPU provisioning failures in eu-west1. Kibana shows the provisioner error lines, but the trace_id is missing on most entries so I can't correlate with the runtime logs. Anybody else?

ryan: can you paste an example trace id you tried and a sample log?

sasha: example trace id I have from the API call: 7f3a9b12c4d6. Searching Kibana for that returns only the api-gateway entry. provisioner and kubelet logs do not show it. Here's a snippet from provisioner stdout (copied):

```
time="2026-02-28T08:12:03Z" level=error msg="provision failed" node=eu-west1-gpu-12 reason="insufficient resources" req_id=7f3a9b12c4d6 details="requested 4 gpus, available 0"
```

and from kubelet on same timeframe we get:

```
Feb 28 08:12:04 eu-west1-gpu-12 kubelet[1]: E0328 08:12:04.123 kubelet.go:123] pod start failed: image pull backoff
```

Notice kubelet line has no req_id/trace info.

jordan: two quick guesses: 1) multiline / line-splitting issue (trace on a different line), 2) ingestion filter that drops the `req_id` field on some nodes (fluent-bit filter/remove_keys or a parsers.conf mismatch).

loki-bot: alert: loki_query_error rate increased for query="{app=\"provisioner\"} |= \"provision failed\"" (5m)

ryan: can you run a Loki query that captures raw logs around that pod to see if trace_id is getting emitted but on the *previous* log line? try: 

```
{job="kubernetes"} |= "eu-west1-gpu-12" |= "provision" | line_format "{{ .raw }}" | count_over_time(1m)
```

sasha: ran something similar. I realized many provisioner logs are multiline — stack traces and context appended after the first line. Our fluent-bit multiline parser is only enabled for the `docker` parser on some nodes; the CRI parser config wasn't applied on the nodepool that hosts GPUs.

sasha: example of paired lines I saw in raw file:

```
[2026-02-28T08:12:03Z] ERROR provisioner: provision failed req_id=7f3a9b12c4d6
  stack: runtime.go:234 -> provision.go:98 -> scheduler.go:54
```

kubelet and container logs are split into two events at ingestion. Our Kibana queries are single-line searches, so the `req_id` sometimes ends up in the second event and is not matched.

ryan: that would explain why only API shows the id consistently (API emits single-line). Two follow-ups: 1) enable the CRI multiline parser on the GPU nodepool fluent-bit daemonset, 2) add an extraction filter to promote `req_id` to a label in Loki during ingest so queries can match even if line splitting remains for a day.

jordan: for the extraction filter, something like: 

```
[FILTER]
    Name    record_modifier
    Match   kube.*
    Record  req_id ${REQ_ID}
```

But better is to use `lua` or `regex` filter to extract `req_id` from the raw and set it as a label before sending to loki. Example regex in fluent-bit: `req_id=(?<req_id>[0-9a-f]{12})`.

ops-oncall: we should also adjust the Grafana SLO panels showing "provisioner error rate by trace" — right now they rely on `req_id` in message text. If we surface `req_id` as a label (loki label), those dashboards will be more robust and alerting cheaper.

sasha: plan:
- I'll open a PR to apply the CRI multiline parser to the gpu nodepool fluent-bit DaemonSet (sasha).
- Ryan will prototype a fluent-bit regex filter to extract `req_id` and attach it as a label before Loki (ryan).
- Jordan will update Grafana panels/alerting to use `req_id` label instead of parsing message text (jordan).

ryan: quick Loki query I tested that helped find split events:

```
{app="provisioner"} |= "provision failed" | line_format "{{ .raw }}" | regexp "req_id=([0-9a-f]{12})"
```

That returned both single-line and split events when run against raw ingestion. Once we propagate `req_id` as a label, we can do faster: `{app="provisioner", req_id="7f3a9b12c4d6"}`

sasha: FYI I also found two nodes with an older fluent-bit image that didn't include our custom multiline parser, so there's a rolling upgrade required. I'll include that in the PR.

jordan: also add a short-term dashboard query to estimate how many events per hour are missing `req_id` by counting `provision failed` hits without `req_id` in the raw. That gives us a roll-forward metric to see fix effect.

devops-bot: deploy approved for daemonset patch. CI checks pending.

sasha: thanks — I'll link the PR once created and post a follow-up when the patch has rolled to 100% of gpu nodes. If anyone wants to triage errors in the meantime, search Loki with the regex above to surface split events. :thumbsup:

ryan: small note — if we enable label extraction, keep an eye on cardinality. `req_id` is high-cardinality by design, but scoped queries (job + req_id) are fine; avoid adding it to wide-indexed dashboards.

jordan: agreed. we'll only create req_id as a label for the provisioner stream, not globally.

ops-oncall: marking as incident follow-up, adding to postmortem board.

sasha: closing the loop: PR opened (link pasted), rolling to 50% now. I'll update thread when at 100%.
